definitions.explanation: Previously worn clothing that is sold or given away.

examples.japanese: フリーマーケットで{古着|ふるぎ}を{売|う}る。
examples.english: To sell used clothes at a flea market.

examples.japanese: {古着|ふるぎ}{屋|や}で{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの}を{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: I found a bargain at the secondhand clothing store.

notes:
{古着|ふるぎ} refers to secondhand or used clothing. It is neutral in tone — it does not imply the clothing is worn out or low quality.

FORMS:
{古|ふる} (old, used) + {着|ぎ} (clothing, from {着|き}る "to wear"). Note the rendaku: {着|き} becomes {着|ぎ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古着|ふるぎ}{屋|や}: secondhand clothing store
- {古着|ふるぎ}を{買|か}う: to buy used clothes
- {古着|ふるぎ}を{売|う}る: to sell used clothes

CULTURAL NOTE:
{古着|ふるぎ} shopping is popular in Japan, especially among younger people. Famous areas include {下北沢|しもきたざわ} in {東京|とうきょう} and {堀江|ほりえ} in {大阪|おおさか}. The term covers both affordable thrift items and curated vintage fashion.

SIMILAR:
- {中古|ちゅうこ}: secondhand (for goods in general, not clothing-specific)
- {古本|ふるほん}: used books (same {古|ふる}～ pattern)
